what_this_is: The Workshop row that uploads one file from a folder the person granted to a signed storage slot a hosted page hands over, only when the slot fits a destination row of read-data/guarded-upload.json; the page learns the size, never the bytes.

payload.label: Upload a file to a signed storage slot
payload.job: Upload one file from a folder the person granted to a signed storage slot a page hands over, only to a destination the tool's own list allows, so the page never sees the file
payload.description: Give file (its name inside the folder the person granted this tool, such as reports/diag.zip), content_type (the file's media type) and slot ({ url, fields }: the https address and the text form fields the storage service signed). The slot is checked as a whole before a byte leaves: https, a host equal to a destination row's, a path inside that row's folder, no query, fragment, credentials or port, text-only fields within the row's field cap, and a content type the row lists. The file is read from the granted folder only (a name that leaves it, or a link out of it, names nothing), held once, and posted as the form's last field. Returns sent, size and said; the signed fields are never in an answer or an error. The shipped destination list is empty, so it uploads nowhere until a destination row is added to read-data/guarded-upload.json.

laid_files.text: {"_what":"Where a page may have this computer upload a file for it (read-data/guarded-upload.mjs, run by the Workshop row tool:upload-a-file-to-a-signed-slot). The page cannot send a local file anywhere itself (the browser's cross-origin rules forbid it), so it asks this program, handing over a signed storage slot (an address and the form fields the storage service signed). The program uploads only to a destination a row here names: https, exactly that host, a path inside that row's folder, no query, no credentials, no port, at most max_fields fields, and a content type the row lists. The file is read from the one folder the person granted this tool (read-a-folder) and the page never sees it, only its size. A new destination is a new row; an empty list uploads nowhere.","destinations":[{"host":"uploads.sample-storage.example","path_prefix":"/sample-bucket/","max_fields":8,"content_types":["text/plain"]}],"hold_minutes":15,"max_hold_bytes":268435456,"words":{"no_such_hold":"That file is not held (it was sent, or its {minutes} minutes ran out).","not_https":"The upload address must be https.","bad_address":"The upload address has a query, credentials, a port or no host, so it was not used.","host_not_allowed":"This computer does not upload to {host}.","path_not_allowed":"The upload path is outside the folder this computer allows for {host}.","too_many_fields":"The upload form has {count} fields; at most {max} are allowed.","bad_field":"The upload form field {name} is not text.","type_not_allowed":"This computer does not upload files of type {type} to {host}.","too_big":"The file is {bytes} bytes; at most {max} are held.","refused":"The storage service refused the upload ({status}).","sent":"Uploaded {bytes} bytes.","no_folder":"No folder is granted to this tool, so there is no file to upload.","outside_folder":"{file} is not a file inside the folder granted to this tool.","no_such_file":"{file} is not a file in the folder granted to this tool."}}
